results.corrected_title: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps run 1,946 GPT-Rosalind agents over a mouse-brain CRISPR atlas in 32 minutes
results.corrected_summary: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research ran 1,946 GPT-Rosalind agents in parallel over a whole-brain CRISPR atlas covering millions of mouse brain cells. The analysis took 32 minutes. Working without the original study's manuscript, the agents matched or refined 48 of its 55 findings and produced new hypotheses, such as a link between DCTN1 and neuronal cholesterol regulation. The results are in a bioRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the hypotheses have not been tested in the lab.
key_facts: 1,946 GPT-Rosalind agents ran in parallel, finishing in 32 minutes
Agents matched or refined 48 of the 55 findings in the original atlas study, without access to its manuscript
Distributed agents kept 7,586 references; single-agent runs averaged about 11
The 'months to a year' human-time comparison is illustrative, built on assumed task times
bioRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed; hypotheses such as DCTN1 and cholesterol still need lab validation
results.issues: The TechRepublic and OpenAI pages returned 403 and could not be opened; the OpenAI URL was only seen in search results. All key figures were confirmed by R&D World and match secondary coverage. PerturbAI first released the atlas itself in March 2026; only the agent analysis is new.

results.corrected_title: Claude autonomously designs 17 scorpion-toxin binders in a 64-hour protein-design campaign
results.corrected_summary: Anthropic reported a 64-hour protein-design campaign run by Claude from one initial prompt and four follow-ups. Claude used 12 design tools and about 10,000 GPU hours to generate 318,484 designs. Of 211 designs tested in the lab by Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience, 17 bound one of five scorpion neurotoxins, and the two best Cn2 binders had single-digit nanomolar affinity. Anthropic says it has not shown that the binders neutralise venom and does not claim an antivenom.
key_facts: 64 hours in total, from 1 prompt plus 4 follow-ups
318,484 designs generated with 12 tools and about 10,000 GPU hours
17 of 211 tested designs bound a toxin (Cn2: 7, AaH II: 4, AaH I: 4, LqhIII: 2); none of the multitoxin designs qualified
The two best Cn2 binders (Cn2-B1, Cn2-B2) had single-digit nanomolar KD
Not tested for neutralisation in cells or animals; binding was tested only against recombinant toxins
results.issues: All figures were confirmed against the primary Anthropic page. The AI Weekly page was not opened. Minor point: of the 211 tested designs, 180 were chosen by Claude and 31 were added with Claude's help, so the selection was not fully autonomous.

results.corrected_title: PHP2Shell: critical PHP flaws found with AI help get emergency patches as exploitation begins
results.corrected_summary: On 21 October PHP shipped emergency patches for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (PHP2Shell). These two critical flaws in PHP core allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and PHP is estimated to run about 70 percent of the web. Researchers from Calif, OpenAI and Wiz found them, and reports say OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol played a key role. Amazon's threat intelligence team saw an exploit attempt on 17 October, before disclosure, and CISA, the UK NCSC, the NSA and the FBI urged organisations to patch.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated CVSS 9.2, allow pre-authentication remote code execution in PHP core
Fixed releases: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; source backports for 7.4 to 8.1
Found by Calif (via OpenAI's Patch the Planet, using GPT-5.6 Sol), OpenAI and Wiz after about two months of coordinated remediation
Amazon saw a first exploit attempt against its honeypot on 17 October; leaked details pushed the release forward a day
CISA, the UK NCSC, the NSA and the FBI issued warnings; Cloudflare deployed WAF rules
results.issues: Several corrections. (1) The 1 billion dollar Daybreak for Frontline Defenders subsidy is not new: Latent Space says it was introduced almost two months earlier, so it is stale and was removed. (2) No source confirms that OpenAI proposed a 'disclosure framework for AI-found bugs'; only The New Stack headline suggests it, and its article body could not be read, so this was removed. (3) 'Affects 70 percent of the web' really means PHP runs an estimated 70 percent of the web. (4) Cloudflare was not a disclosing coalition member; it deployed WAF rules. (5) Credit for the discovery differs between outlets: Wiz also used Gemini 4 Argon, and Calif reportedly found the bugs in August.
